findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_skills, url_to_markdown, json_repair, email_check · Private data: agent_ready_kit, token_count, token_risk, token_price, ip_intel, llm_cost_quote, dns_lookup, whois_rdap · Public sink: json_schema_validate, email_check, name_resolve · Destructive: json_schema_validate, uuid_mint, cron_next.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_skills, url_to_markdown, json_repair, email_check · Private data: agent_ready_kit, token_count, token_risk, token_price, ip_intel, llm_cost_quote, dns_lookup, whois_rdap · Public sink: json_schema_validate, email_check, name_resolve · Destructive: json_schema_validate, uuid_mint, cron_next

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
